short: Pioneering experimental physicist whose discoveries formed the foundation of electromagnetism.
full:
Michael Faraday rose from a humble background with little formal education to become one of the most influential scientists in history. Beginning as an assistant to Humphry Davy at the Royal Institution, his unparalleled skill in experimental chemistry and physics led him to discover electromagnetic induction in 1831, proving that a changing magnetic field could induce an electric current.

His subsequent inventions, including the first electric motor and the early dynamo, demonstrated that electricity could be harnessed for practical mechanical work. Faraday's conceptual breakthroughs regarding magnetic lines of force were later formulated mathematically by James Clerk Maxwell, underpinning the vast electrical infrastructure of the modern world.
